create.gatewayOutside: This gateway is outside the network.

segment.title: New network segment
segment.intro: Declare an address range of a network. Members of the segment's responsible groups may allocate its addresses; your primary group becomes responsible for it. The range must lie inside the network and must not overlap another of its segments.

segment.noRow: The segment was created but not returned.

create.title: New group
create.intro: A privilege group grants a right across the collector. An ordinary group only gathers users, to hold responsibilities.
create.exists: A group named {{role}} already exists. Creating it again would modify it.

delete.question: Delete the group {{role}}? Its memberships, responsibilities and publications go with it. This cannot be undone.

create.title: New tag
create.intro: A tag marks nodes and services, to group them in filters and views. Only its name is required.
create.excludeHint: Regular expression of the tag names that cannot be attached along with this one. Optional.
create.excludeInvalid: This is not a valid regular expression.
create.dataHint: Free data attached to the tag, in JSON. Optional.

delete.label: Delete the user
delete.question: Delete the user {{email}}?
delete.consequence: Their team memberships, private team, identity provider links, session filter and preferences go with the account; the audit log and the history of their actions stay. They can no longer sign in. This cannot be undone.

detail.title: User
detail.editHint: A user may change their own name and email; changing another user's requires the UserManager privilege. The email is the sign-in name.

memberships.hint: Changing the groups of a user requires the GroupManager privilege; unless you are a Manager, you can only add groups you are a member of.

create.title: New user
create.intro: The collector also creates the user's private group. Only the email is required.
create.noPassword: Without a password the account exists but cannot sign in.

groups.title: Groups and privileges
groups.hint: Your organizational groups decide which nodes, services and applications you see; your privilege groups decide what you may change. A GroupManager changes them from the Users view; when you sign in through your identity provider, some may follow its claims.
groups.manager: Manager grants every privilege: the other privilege groups add nothing to it.

palette.title: Theme
palette.hint: High contrast uses black or white text, visible borders and saturated colours. Colour-blind friendly shows the states in blue, gold and crimson rather than green and red. Both apply in light as in dark mode.

theme.title: Light or dark

obsolescence.title: Obsolescence
obsolescence.intro: Warning and alert dates for each hardware model and OS release reported by nodes. The collector applies them to the matching nodes and raises dashboard alerts when they are reached.

refresh.done: Settings are up to date with the inventory.

detail.title: Obsolescence setting
detail.editHint: Only the deadlines can be changed; clearing one removes it. A change applies to the matching nodes and updates their obsolescence alerts on the dashboard.

charts.title: Charts
charts.intro: Time series of historized metrics, each defined in YAML, which reports show. A Manager sees every chart; the others see the charts published to one of their teams.

form.title: New chart
form.intro: The chart is published to your primary team, which is also made responsible for it. Creating a chart requires the ReportsManager privilege.
form.yamlPlaceholder:
Metrics:
  - metric_id: 186
    label: Nodes by OS
Options:
  stack: true
form.yamlHint: Optional: the definition can be written later. It must be valid YAML: the historized metrics drawn (metric_id) and the Options.

reports.title: Report definitions
reports.intro: Pages of charts and metrics, each defined in YAML. A Manager sees every report; the others see the reports published to one of their teams. They are read in Statistics › Reports.

preview.noHistory: No history yet: the collector records the metrics once a day.
preview.notice: Preview of the report: each metric is run now. Its placeholders stand for the nodes and services you can see, narrowed by your session filter.
preview.empty: The report has no definition yet: write one to preview it.

form.title: New report
form.intro: The report is published to your primary team, which is also made responsible for it. Creating a report requires the ReportsManager privilege.
form.yamlHint: Optional: the definition can be written later. It must be valid YAML.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.intro: SQL requests whose results feed the charts and the reports. A historized metric is computed every day and its values kept over time.

form.createIntro: The metric is published to your primary team, so that its members see it. Creating a metric requires the Manager privilege.
form.editIntro: Charts and reports using the metric read it with the new definition. Editing requires the Manager privilege.
form.sqlPlaceholder: SELECT os_name, COUNT(*) FROM nodes WHERE node_id IN (%%fset_node_ids%%) GROUP BY os_name
form.sqlHint: %%fset_node_ids%% and %%fset_svc_ids%% stand for the nodes and services of the filterset of the session where the metric is read.
form.indexHint: Columns of the result, counted from 0. Leave the instance column empty when the request returns a single value.
form.historizeHint: The collector computes the metric every day and keeps its values for the charts.

filters.title: Filters
filters.intro: A filter is one condition on a column of a collector table. Filtersets combine filters to select nodes and services.

form.editIntro: Filtersets using this filter will select according to the new definition.
form.valueHint: With LIKE, % matches any text. With IN, separate values with commas.

delete.question: Delete the filter {{label}}? This cannot be undone.

filtersets.title: Filtersets
filtersets.intro: A filterset combines filters, and other filtersets, with logical operators. Views and compliance rulesets use filtersets to select nodes and services.

claimMappings.title: Claim mappings
claimMappings.intro: Rules translating the claims your identity provider sends at sign-in into access to the collector and teams. A rule matches when the claim equals the value, or, for a list such as groups, contains it. Once a rule allows signing in, only the identities matching one may sign in through the provider, and those may have their account created at their first sign-in. The teams a rule names follow the claims at every sign-in; the others are managed in Teams. Signing in with a collector password is not affected.

current.title: Claims of your current sign-in
current.intro: What your identity provider sent when you signed in. Click a value to start a rule from it.
current.notOidc: You signed in with a collector password: there are no claims to show. Sign in through the identity provider to see the claims it sends.
current.none: Your sign-in carries no claim a rule could use.

form.intro: The rule applies at the next sign-in of each account, and at once to the Bearer tokens of scripts.
form.claimHint: The claim name as the provider sends it (groups, email, roles…), or a dotted path into a nested claim (realm_access.roles).
form.valueHint: Compared exactly, case included. For a list, the rule matches when the list contains this value.
form.accessHint: Once at least one rule allows signing in, the identities matching none are refused, even with an existing account.
form.teamHint: As many groups as needed. Everybody and the private groups of the users cannot be granted.
form.noEffect: Choose at least one effect: allow signing in, or grant teams.
form.teamWarning_one: {{teams}} will follow the claims: at their next sign-in through the provider, the accounts matching no rule granting it leave it, even if they were added by hand.
form.teamWarning_other: {{teams}} will follow the claims: at their next sign-in through the provider, the accounts matching no rule granting one of them leave it, even if they were added by hand.

kindHint.org: What the matching accounts see: the nodes, services and applications of these groups.

delete.consequence: The accounts the rules put in a team no other rule names leave it at once; those added by hand stay, and the team is managed by hand again. The teams other rules still name follow the claims at the next sign-in of each account.
